response.sql:
WITH state_counts AS (
    SELECT c.state_county_province, COUNT(*) AS account_count
    FROM Accounts AS a
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.state_county_province
), state_shares AS (
    SELECT state_county_province,
           account_count,
           CAST(account_count AS DECIMAL(30,10)) / SUM(account_count) OVER () AS share
    FROM state_counts
), scored_states AS (
    SELECT state_county_province,
           account_count,
           share,
           AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share
    FROM state_shares
)
SELECT SUM(account_count) AS combined_count,
       AVG(share) AS average_share,
       AVG(share - average_share) AS average_excess_share
FROM scored_states
WHERE share > average_share

assumptions.assumption: A state/province value of NULL is treated as the single missing-state group, as with SQL GROUP BY.
